//: Deno config used ONLY by `npm run typecheck:edge` (scripts/typecheck-edge.mjs).
//nodeModulesDir: The repo root has a package.json, so Deno would otherwise switch to node_modules resolution and fail on every `npm:` specifier that is not an npm dependency of the WEB app (@react-email/components, resend, react). Edge functions run on Supabase's Deno runtime with no node_modules, so resolve npm: from Deno's global cache exactly like production does.
//lock: Deliberately off. The root deno.lock belongs to other tooling, and a second lock here would have to be regenerated by hand every time an edge function adds an import - which is exactly the kind of opt-in step that let edge functions go unchecked in the first place. Determinism comes from the pinned versions in the import specifiers themselves (stripe@18.5.0, std@0.190.0, ...).
//location: This file lives in scripts/ rather than being named deno.json so that no stray `deno` invocation elsewhere in the repo auto-discovers it, and so it can never alter how `supabase functions deploy` bundles these files.
//imports: TYPES ONLY - production still loads the esm.sh build untouched. esm.sh serves Stripe's .d.ts files but they are wrapped in `declare module 'https://esm.sh/stripe@18.5.0/types/index.d.ts'`, which does not match the specifier the functions import, so every Stripe call resolved to `any` and the current_period_end bug was invisible even with the types downloaded. See scripts/edge-types/stripe-18.5.0.ts. If this key ever stops matching the URL the functions import, Stripe silently reverts to `any` - scripts/typecheck-edge.mjs asserts the mapping is live before reporting success.
